name: Elira
occupation: Former Tally-Recorder / Keeper of the Counting-Signs / Unassigned (officially erased from civic rolls)
bloodline: Unregistered (formerly attached to the Assembly's record office, clan-name struck from the tally-rolls)
residence: Abandoned house at the edge of the Lower Town, near the dried Old Canal Bed
personality: never fully trusts any single explanation
notices what people avoid more than what they say
daily_routine: copying old counts and Sign-sequences from memory into private notebooks
observing movement patterns across the Citadel and Lower Town from a distance
rarely entering the Great Court unless approached first
collecting discarded or lost record fragments left in the dried canal silt
monitoring changes in Assembly and Great Bath behavior
avoiding direct interaction unless approached first

goals.hidden_goal: Preserve a complete reconstruction of pre-Turning administrative records and map the inconsistencies between official history and physical evidence
goals.deep_goal: Understand why certain records were systematically removed rather than merely lost

beliefs: Absence of records is itself meaningful
Systems erase what they fear will be reinterpreted
Memory exists in both people and structures, not just in tally-rolls
The Assembly is not hiding the truth about the Turning; it is managing it
